definitions.explanation: A self-destructive frame of mind that arises when things do not go as one hoped, leading one to give up and act without regard for the consequences.

examples.english: Give in to despair; act out of desperation.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちて、やけになってしまった。
examples.english: I failed the exam and fell into despair.

examples.japanese: うまくいかないからといって、やけを{起|お}こしても{何|なに}も{解決|かいけつ}しない。
examples.english: Even if things aren't going well, lashing out in desperation won't solve anything.

notes:
Usually written in kana, though the kanji form is {自棄|やけ}. Describes the state of "giving up" and behaving recklessly out of frustration or hopelessness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- やけになる: to become desperate; to give up in despair
- やけを{起|お}こす: to act rashly out of despair
- やけ{酒|ざけ}: drowning one's sorrows in drink
- やけ{食|ぐ}い: stress eating; binge eating out of frustration

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自暴自棄|じぼうじき}: self-destructive recklessness — the four-character idiom expressing the same idea more formally
